problem: Modular object navigation frameworks rely on instance segmentation models trained at a fixed camera height, so they generalize poorly to other viewpoint heights and each new height needs costly new labels.
motivation: Robots of different form factors have cameras at different heights, so the segmentation module that feeds semantic mapping degrades when the height changes. Labeling data for every new height is expensive, so transferring knowledge from a labeled source height to an unlabeled target height with few labels is attractive.
key_idea: A semi-supervised teacher-student framework transfers instance segmentation knowledge from a source camera height to a target height using a projection policy for the teacher, confidence-based dynamic weighting of pseudo-labels, and prototype contrastive transfer.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract suggests that the viewpoint-height gap can be bridged by improving the teacher's pseudo-labels at the target height (projection policy) and by down-weighting low-confidence pseudo-labels to limit overfitting.
method: Projection policy: enhances the teacher model's detection capability at the target height
Dynamic weight mechanism: weights pseudo-labels by confidence so high-confidence ones dominate, reducing overfitting to noisy labels
Prototype contrast transferring: uses prototype-based contrastive learning to transfer class knowledge from source to target height
Semi-supervised teacher-student training: uses a labeled source height and mostly unlabeled target height data to minimize additional labels

setting.backbone: instance segmentation model in a teacher-student setup (specific architecture not stated in abstract)
setting.training_data: HM3D images at a source camera height with labels plus target height images mostly unlabeled (scale not given in abstract)
